column1: You configure DAB to expose dbo.Products. What two types of API can DAB generate for it?
column2:
REST and GraphQL APIs without a custom API implementation.
For example, point DAB at dbo.Products and configure a Product entity. DAB generates endpoints for that entity, but the configuration still determines which operations each role can use.
Review source

column1: Which DAB configuration property enables editor validation and IntelliSense for the JSON file?
column2:
$schema.
An editor uses the schema to suggest valid keys and flag unknown properties. Match the schema version to the engine so the editor does not suggest settings that the deployed version cannot use.
Review source

column1: Which DAB configuration section maps named API resources to tables, views, or stored procedures?
column2:
entities.
An entity is a named API resource backed by a database object. For example, a Product entity can point to dbo.Products and grant a role read access without exposing other tables.
Review source

column1: Which DAB database-type value supports SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, and SQL database in Fabric?
column2:
mssql.
The value selects the Microsoft SQL connection provider. The connection string identifies the actual server and database, so mssql alone does not choose between Azure SQL Database and SQL database in Fabric.
Review source

column1: Which DAB option makes caller claims available to SQL code through SESSION_CONTEXT()?
column2:
data-source.options.set-session-context.
This option makes caller claims available to SQL code through SESSION_CONTEXT(). SQL can then use those claims in a row-level security rule. The option does not create that rule.
Review source

column1: DAB uses /api as its REST base path and Product as its entity path. What URL path lists products?
column2:
/api/Product.
Join the configured REST base path to the configured entity path. This URL addresses the collection. A URL for one row also needs that row's key.
Review source

column1: What can a client discover by running GraphQL introspection against DAB?
column2:
The API's schema, including its types and fields.
Introspection lets a client ask which types, fields, and operations the schema defines. Turning it off limits discovery, but does not stop authorized clients from running queries they already know.
Review source

column1: In DAB, what does runtime.host.cors.origins let you control for browser requests from another site?
column2:
Which browser origins can access cross-origin API responses.
An origin consists of the scheme, host, and port. The CORS setting tells the browser which other origins can read the response. It does not authorize requests from nonbrowser clients.
Review source

column1: Which DAB host mode is intended for deployed production services?
column2:
production.
Production mode is for the deployed service. Development mode is useful during local troubleshooting, but its extra diagnostics are not meant for public use. Production mode does not replace entity permissions.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0, what default does runtime.cache.ttl-seconds set for cached REST responses?
column2:
The default lifetime of cached REST results, in seconds.
TTL means time to live. After this interval, an entry is no longer fresh. An entity can override the runtime value, and the DAB 2.0 response cache applies to REST, not GraphQL.
Review source

column1: A DAB REST request body contains an unknown field. What happens when request-body-strict is true?
column2:
It rejects the request with a BadRequest error.
Strict mode can catch a typo such as Prcie instead of Price. If strict mode is disabled, DAB ignores the unknown field rather than treating it as a valid entity property.
Review source

column1: What access does --permissions "anonymous:read" grant to a DAB entity?
column2:
Read access without requiring caller authentication.
This role lets an unauthenticated caller read the entity. It does not grant create, update, or delete access. Use it only when the exposed data is meant to be public.
Review source

column1: What part of DAB's connection configuration can you commit to Git without committing the credential?
column2:
Nonsecret configuration containing references to securely supplied credentials.
Commit the entity definitions and a reference such as @env('DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING'). Supply the actual value at runtime so the team can review the configuration without putting credentials in Git.
Review source

column1: The DAB base file and the selected environment file both set the connection string. Which value takes precedence?
column2:
The environment-specific value.
The environment variant overrides matching settings. The base file still supplies keys that the variant does not override. This lets deployments share entity definitions while varying environment settings.
Review source

column1: What happens to an existing DAB configuration file when you run dab init against that file?
column2:
The existing file is overwritten, not merged.
dab init writes a fresh baseline rather than adding settings to an existing file. Run it against a different output file if you want to keep the current entity definitions.
Review source

column1: Which DAB REST query parameter requests up to 25 records per page?
column2:
$first=25.
This sets an upper bound for the requested page, not a guarantee of 25 results. Fewer rows can match the filter or remain on the last page.
Review source

column1: A DAB REST collection has more results. Which response property contains the URL to fetch the next page?
column2:
nextLink.
The nextLink URL carries the continuation information for the current result. Follow it as returned to resume after this page rather than trying to create or decode $after yourself.
Review source

column1: Which DAB setting limits how large a page clients can request, rather than setting the default page size?
column2:
runtime.pagination.max-page-size.
This setting caps a caller's requested page size. If a positive $first exceeds the limit, DAB rejects the request instead of silently lowering the requested size.
Review source

column1: Which DAB setting supplies the REST page size if the client omits $first?
column2:
runtime.pagination.default-page-size.
The default fills in the page size when the client does not ask for one. The documented default is 100. The maximum setting separately caps how much the client can request.
Review source

column1: Which DAB REST query parameter restricts rows by a condition?
column2:
$filter.
The filter changes which rows qualify. For example, Price ge 10 includes a price of exactly 10 and excludes 9. Use $select instead to choose the fields returned.
Review source

column1: How does a DAB REST filter select rows whose Rating is NULL?
column2:
$filter=Rating eq null.
Use eq null to ask for a missing SQL value. Quoting null instead asks for the literal text null, which is not the same as a missing value.
Review source

column1: Which DAB REST query parameter sorts rows by Price descending?
column2:
$orderby=Price desc.
The desc modifier puts higher prices first. If two rows share a price and their order matters, add a unique field such as Id as a second sort key.
Review source

column1: Which DAB REST query parameter returns only the Id and Name fields?
column2:
$select=Id,Name.
The selection limits which fields appear in each result object. It does not change which rows match or give the caller access to fields that the role cannot read.
Review source

column1: Which DAB GraphQL argument requests up to 25 records per page?
column2:
first: 25.
Put first on the collection field, not inside its selection set. It limits how many items the page can contain. The last page can contain fewer.
Review source

column1: Which DAB GraphQL field indicates that more records remain after the current page?
column2:
hasNextPage.
Ask for hasNextPage alongside items. If the flag is true, use the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than inferring more results from the item count.
Review source

column1: A DAB GraphQL response shows that more records remain. How do you use its cursor to continue?
column2:
Pass the returned endCursor value to the next query's after argument.
The cursor marks where the next query resumes. Pass it back unchanged and keep the same filter and sort so you continue through the same result set.
Review source

column1: Which DAB GraphQL filter finds titles containing the text SQL?
column2:
filter: { title: { contains: "SQL" } }.
The contains condition looks for the supplied text within a title. This can match a longer title such as Learning SQL. It does not rank results by relevance.
Review source

column1: Which DAB 2.0 setting must you enable at runtime before any entity can cache REST responses?
column2:
runtime.cache.enabled = true.
The runtime switch enables caching for the service, but it does not opt in every entity. Configure caching on each entity whose REST responses you want DAB to cache.
Review source

column1: The DAB 2.0 runtime cache is on. Which setting opts the Product entity into REST response caching?
column2:
Set entities.Product.cache.enabled to true.
The Product setting opts this entity into REST response caching. The runtime switch must remain enabled. Other entities do not opt in just because Product does.
Review source
